name: Movie Recap Paragraph Scene Workflow
use_when: The user wants a movie recap, movie explainer, anime recap, episode recap, or scene-by-scene commentary from a full movie or long source.
The edit uses fresh narration over muted source footage.
The project needs short social-ready recap units rather than a full linear retelling.
The agent needs to map narration paragraphs to exact source scenes.
avoid_when: The user wants a full-length review with host commentary and no scene montage.
The source footage is not available for visual matching.
The user explicitly asks for one continuous long recap instead of short paragraph units.

timeline_pattern.pattern: movie_title_year -> gripping_section_selection -> paragraph_script -> scene_hint -> visual_verification -> one_paragraph_short
timeline_pattern.release_year_rule: Include the movie release year when requesting or researching plot sections so the correct title/version is used.
timeline_pattern.paragraph_rule: Write compact narration paragraphs. Each paragraph must have a scene target, source range hint, and visual job.
timeline_pattern.short_unit_rule: Default to one paragraph per exported short. Use multiple paragraph exports as a series rather than one long video unless the user asks otherwise.
timeline_pattern.scene_match_rule: Use AI-proposed timestamps only as hints. Verify the actual movie frames before cutting.

motion.rule: Let motion treatment follow the paragraph's tension: calmer setup can hold a little longer, danger/action paragraphs need faster fragments and stronger visual changes.
motion.avoid: Adding motion graphics that distract from the movie moment the narration is explaining.

sound.rule: Movie source audio is muted by default. The generated/recorded narration is the main audio, with optional low music or subtle SFX below it.
sound.avoid: Leaving original dialogue, score, or effects under the recap narration by accident.

captions.rule: If captions are requested, caption the recap narration, not the movie's original dialogue.
captions.avoid: Letting captions cover the source action or burn-in movie subtitles.

color.rule: Grade lightly for consistency across fragments while preserving scene readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create an EDL per paragraph with verified source ranges, muted source audio, voiceover as the primary audio, and short transformed visual fragments. Export each paragraph as its own short unless the user asks for a combined render.
implementation.remotion: Represent each paragraph as a data object with script, sourceSceneHint, verifiedRanges, visualFragments, voiceover, captions, and outputFormat.
implementation.blender: Use only for special explanatory inserts or stylized scene cards; the core recap remains source-footage fragments matched to narration.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place the paragraph voiceover first, import the movie, find the matching source scene, mute the video, then cut visuals to the paragraph.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers for each paragraph, source time hints, verified source ranges, and narration beats. Keep each paragraph in its own sequence for export.

common_mistakes: Writing a full movie summary before deciding which gripping section the short is about.
Combining all generated paragraphs into a longer video by default.
Trusting AI timestamps without checking the actual movie frames.
Dragging the whole movie under the voiceover and trimming randomly instead of finding the matching scene.
Letting source audio compete with narration.
qc: Does each paragraph have a verified matching scene or scene range?
Is each final export short enough to feel like one focused recap unit?
Is the source movie audio muted?
Does the narration explain the scene currently on screen?
Have all AI-generated scene hints been checked visually?
Does the final file use the requested aspect ratio and platform format?
